title: How a hurricane forms
why: A natural process unfolds in time, so chronological order lets listeners follow cause to result.
pieces: Attention: "Every hurricane begins as a patch of warm, ordinary-looking ocean."
Preview: "Let's follow a storm from warm water to a named hurricane in three stages."
I. Warm ocean water evaporates and rises, carrying heat and moisture into the air.
II. Thunderstorms cluster, and Earth's rotation starts the air spinning.
III. When sustained winds reach 74 miles per hour, the storm is classified as a hurricane.
Clincher: "The next time you see a forecast cone, you'll know the journey that storm has already taken."

title: Cutting food waste in our cafeteria
why: The solution should address the cause, so the cause must come before it.
pieces: Attention: a photo description of one day's untouched lunches in the trash.
I. Problem: our cafeteria throws away a large share of the food it serves each day.
II. Cause: students must take every item on the tray, even items they will not eat.
III. Solution: an "offer versus serve" option and a share table for unopened items.
Call to action: "Sign the petition at lunch this week to bring this to the student council."

title: Join the school blood drive
why: Monroe's sequence follows the questions listeners ask as they are persuaded: Why listen? What is wrong? What fixes it? What will it look like? What do I do?
pieces: Attention: the story of a classmate who needed a transfusion after an accident.
Need: regional hospitals regularly report blood shortages, especially in winter and summer.
Satisfaction: one donation can be separated into components that help more than one patient.
Visualization: picture next month: our donations on the shelf when someone in our town needs them.
Action: "Sign up at the library table by Friday. If you're under the age limit, recruit an adult."
